problem: The company wanted to update its brand look.
title: Gap launches a new logo and reverts to the old one within a week
context: In early October 2010 Gap replaced its classic blue box logo on its website and said it would seek customer ideas for improving the design.
decision_made: Roll out a new logo, then return to the original blue box after the reaction.
action_taken: Gap said all roads were leading back to the blue box and conceded that crowdsourcing ideas had not been the best move.
observed_outcome: After online protests the company reverted to the original logo about six days after the change.
lessons: Visible changes to a familiar identity can be reversed quickly under public pressure, and inviting input late can look like indecision.
limitations: Sources differ slightly on dates. The business effect of the episode was not measured in the sources used.

claims.claim_text: Gap said it would keep the classic blue box logo and stop using the new one.
Gap reverted to its original logo after an outcry, and conceded crowdsourcing was not the best move.
